title: VPC probe degradation hunter and safe IaC reconcile: runbook + automated remediations
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Proactive runbook and automated remediation for progressive VPC probe degradations that begin as intermittent probe timeouts and can escalate to sustained node-level health failures. Integrates Terraform drift detection + safe reconcile steps, canary upgrade gating, and a lightweight anomaly hunter that proposes action (cordon/taint/recreate, rollback, Terraform replan) rather than immediately performing high-risk operations. Goal: reduce P1 escalations by surfacing safe automated fixes and an operator-friendly playbook for on-call engineers.
runbook_steps: 1) Triage: on alert, open incident channel and record affected cluster/region and customer IDs.
2) Snapshot current state: run `tfstate show` and `kubectl get nodes -o wide` and upload to the incident doc.
3) Confirm degradation scope: run synthetic probe summary (last 60m) and compare to baseline histogram in Grafana.
4) Run quick remediation decision tree: if >50% nodes failing healthchecks -> follow mass-failure flow (escalate + safe rollback); if single node flapping -> candidate for cordon/taint and recreate.
5) Apply safe actions: cordon + drain (with grace period) -> scale replacement node (Terraform apply with `-target` to avoid broad changes) -> monitor KV cache warmup and probe recovery.
6) If remediation fails twice, trigger canary rollback of last platform change and open a postmortem with owner region-ops.
7) Post-incident: capture root cause candidates, add Terraform drift markers, and add automated checks to the anomaly hunter if novel pattern seen.
8) Communication: update customer status dashboard and incident channel with ETA and mitigation steps.
automation_playbook: Anomaly hunter process (daemon): subscribes to probe metrics stream and evaluates deviation score using EWMA + recent error bursts; on score > threshold it executes a read-only investigation (collect logs, tfstate diff, kernel/CUDA mismatch check) and prepares a candidate action in the operator queue.
Operator queue: actions are proposed as labeled tickets with `safe`, `medium`, or `danger` level. Only `safe` actions can be auto-executed when on-call is in auto-remediation mode.

Safe auto-remediation actions: 1) drain + recreate single flapping node; 2) rotate network interface on node (re-attach ENI) if ENI error pattern detected; 3) extend probe timeout for transient network blips and schedule follow-up evaluation.

Medium-risk automated proposals: 1) Terraform replan for drifted module with human approval; 2) perform canary restart of control-plane adjacent service; these require one reviewer approval in Slack/PR before execution.
High-risk actions (never auto-run): mass Terraform apply that affects routing or persistent volumes, full cluster reboot; these must follow rollback gating and SRE approval.

Terraform integration: automation exports `tfplan` diffs to a review PR and tags resources for targeted reapply using `-target` flags when safe. A broker service records `last_safe_plan` per environment for rollbacks.
Reconciliation controller: runs a two-step reconcile - dry-run plan -> risk-check -> either auto-apply (safe) or create review PR (unsafe).
alerts_and_thresholds: probe_timeout_rate > 1% sustained over 10m -> P0 candidate alert to oncall
probe_error_burst > 100 errors in 2m from same AZ -> create operator queue action
node_liveness_failures > 2 nodes in cluster in 5m -> immediate escalated incident
drift_detection: Terraform plan shows >3 resource diffs -> create review PR (risk-high)
kernel_cudnn_mismatch: if `nvidia-smi` driver version != expected -> flag medium risk
rollback_criteria: New change introduced in last 30 minutes and probe error rate doubled -> eligible for automatic rollback of last safe plan
Auto-remediation fails to restore probe success rate within 15 minutes -> trigger manual review
KV cache miss ratio not reduced after node replacement -> do not rollback other nodes; escalate to SRE
commands_and_snippets: Capture state: `terraform state pull > incident-tfstate.json && kubectl get nodes -o wide > nodes-before.txt`

Safe cordon & recreate: `kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60` then `terraform apply -target=module.private_node.aws_instance.node["<id>"]`
Replan for review: `TF_IN_AUTORECONCILE=1 terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan && terraform show -json plan.tfplan > plan.json`
Rewarm KV cache indicator: `redis-cli -h <host> info stats | grep keyspace_hits`
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Auto-recreating nodes during a platform upgrade can land nodes on a mismatched kernel/driver. Mitigation: preflight check that verifies host driver versions before auto-recreate.
Risk: Terraform reapply may touch more resources than intended. Mitigation: always use targeted `-target` applies for auto remediation and require manual PR for broad diffs.
Risk: Auto cordon/drain may cause transient capacity shortage. Mitigation: throttle concurrent auto-remediations and prefer replica creation over mass drain.
Risk: False positives from probe spikes. Mitigation: use burst-resilient EWMA scoring and require sustained deviation window before auto action.
acceptance_criteria: Automation creates proposed actions for >95% of probe degradation alerts and only auto-executes `safe` actions when operator is in auto mode
On-call can approve medium-risk actions from Slack or PR and have the automation execute within 5 minutes
Incidents with this playbook reduce manual escalations for single-node flapping by 60% in the next quarter
Preflight checks block auto-recreate if driver/kernel mismatch risk detected
